title: Microsoft Teams: report a message or an external user for a security concern in US Government clouds
notes: claim 47: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold for a licensing correction: Defender licensing can be included in an existing subscription, not just acquired as an add-on. The roadmap facts and documented reporting controls check out, but the assertion of no new data access is unsubstantiated.

claims.where: controls[0].note

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The report route is Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > User reported security submissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. ... On the View reports tab, under Report, select User reported security submissions.
claims.fix: Include the omitted Report heading: 'Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > User reported security submissions'. The current steps are in the documented order.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default on arrival in GCC, GCC High and DoD is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Report a security concern GCC default'; opened end-user-reporting-security and submissions-teams and read the roadmap. Learn says On by default generally, but its Defender page excludes Gov; none resolves the Gov rollout default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model
claims.claim: The licensing model is add-on.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 (add-on licenses or included in subscriptions like Microsoft 365 E5), admins can also see user reported messages in Microsoft Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'mixed'. Add to the notes: 'Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2 can be acquired as add-on licences or included in subscriptions such as Microsoft 365 E5; a separate add-on is not universally required.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-admin#admin-options-for-user-reported-messages and retain the uncertainty about entitlement for this Government rollout.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Teams reporting page describes organisations with Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report malicious messages in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions: licence
claims.claim: The Defender reporting page also lists Defender for Office 365 Plan 1.
claims.quote: In organizations with Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or Plan 2, or Microsoft Defender XDR, admins can decide whether users can report messages, calls, meetings, or meeting participants in Microsoft Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing

claims.where: What's changing: reporting a message; Governance guidance: At rollout

Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-office-365/submissions-teams#report-malicious-messages-in-teams, which uses that different label for the same reporting flow.

claims.where: rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature gives no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Teams user reporting security new data access permissions'; read end-user-reporting-security, end-user-reported-security-signal and submissions-teams. None establishes no new data access for this Gov rollout; the report documents collected identifiers and participant data.
claims.fix: Remove 'and gives no new data access' from the risk rationale. Retain the verified user-initiated reporting description and the stated uncertainty about Government defaults and data flows.

claims.fix: Remove the After rollout checklist bullet 'Block confirmed malicious external users on the External Access page, using the identifiers in the exported CSV.' It names a blocking control with no table row; the verified explanatory statement in Risk assessment can remain.
